hints.title: State Transition Phase Tracking
hints.text: A frog singing croak transitions through states c -> r -> o -> a -> k sequentially.

hints.title: Letter Precedence Invariance Check
hints.text: Each incoming letter requires an existing frog in the preceding phase. If no frog is in that state, the sequence is invalid.

hints.title: Concurrent Frogs Peak Blueprint
hints.text: When c arrives, start a new frog or recycle a finished frog, and track peak active frogs. When k arrives, the frog finishes and is available for reuse.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def minNumberOfFrogs(self, croakOfFrogs: str) -> int:
        c = r = o = a = 0
        frogs = 0
        max_frogs = 0
        for ch in croakOfFrogs:
            if ch == "c":
                c += 1
                frogs += 1
                max_frogs = max(max_frogs, frogs)
            elif ch == "r":
                if c == 0: return -1
                c -= 1
                r += 1
            elif ch == "o":
                if r == 0: return -1
                r -= 1
                o += 1
            elif ch == "a":
                if o == 0: return -1
                o -= 1
                a += 1
            elif ch == "k":
                if a == 0: return -1
                a -= 1
                frogs -= 1
            else:
                return -1
        return max_frogs if frogs == 0 and c == r == o == a == 0 else -1
```

complexity.notes: Single pass tracking 5 integer phase counters in constant space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Greedy substring search without concurrent phase simulation fails on interleaved croak sounds.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Direct finite state counts eliminate allocating dynamic objects for individual frogs.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Precedence validation and peak concurrent active frog tracking.

solutions.approach: Finite State Machine with Peak Concurrency Counter
